blocks.en: Links
blocks.zh_html: 链路(Links)

blocks.en: Properties of Links
blocks.zh_html: 链路的性质(Properties of Links)

blocks.en: Now that we have a picture of how the layers of the Internet are built, let’s focus on how a packet is sent across a link.
blocks.zh_html: 既然我们已经了解了互联网(Internet)各层的结构，现在让我们聚焦于分组(packet)是如何通过链路(link)发送的。

blocks.en: There are three properties we can use to measure the performance of a link.
blocks.zh_html: 有三个性质(properties)可以用来衡量链路(link)的性能(performance)。

blocks.en: The bandwidth of a link tells us how many bits we can send on the link per unit time. Intuitively, this is the speed of the link. If you think of a link as a pipe carrying water, the bandwidth is the width of the pipe. A wider pipe lets us feed more water into the pipe per second. We usually measure bandwidth in bits per second (e.g. 5 Gbps = 5 billion bits per second).
blocks.zh_html: 链路的带宽(bandwidth)告诉我们每单位时间可以在该链路上发送多少比特(bits)。直观地说，这就是链路的速度。如果你把链路想象成一根输水管，带宽就是管子的宽度。更宽的管子允许我们每秒灌入更多的水。我们通常用比特每秒(bps, bits per second)来衡量带宽，例如 5 Gbps = 50 亿比特每秒。

blocks.en: The propagation delay of a link tells us how long it takes for a bit to travel along the link. In the pipe analogy, this is the length of the link. A shorter pipe means that water spends less time in the pipe before arriving at the other end. Propagation delay is measured in time (e.g. nanoseconds, milliseconds).
blocks.zh_html: 链路的传播时延(propagation delay)告诉我们一个比特(bits)在链路上传输需要多长时间。在管道类比中，这就是管子的长度。较短的管子意味着水在管中到达另一端所花的时间更少。传播时延以时间单位衡量，例如纳秒(nanoseconds)、毫秒(milliseconds)。

blocks.en: If we multiply the bandwidth and the propagation delay, we get the bandwidth-delay product (BDP). Intuitively, this is the capacity of the link, or the number of bits that exist on the link at any given instant. In the pipe analogy, if we fill up the pipe and freeze time, the capacity of the pipe is how much water is in the pipe in that instant.
blocks.zh_html: 将带宽(bandwidth)和传播时延(propagation delay)相乘，就得到带宽时延乘积(BDP, bandwidth-delay product)。直观地说，这就是链路的容量(capacity)，即任意时刻存在于链路上的比特(bits)数量。在管道类比中，如果我们灌满水管然后冻结时间，管道的容量就是那一刻管中的水量。

blocks.en: Note: You might sometimes see the term latency. In the context of a link, the latency is its propagation delay, though this word can also be used in other contexts (e.g. the latency from end host to end host, across multiple links). Latency by itself is not formally defined, and is context-dependent.
blocks.zh_html: 注意：你可能有时会看到术语延迟(latency)。在链路(link)的上下文中，延迟就是传播时延(propagation delay)，不过这个词也可以用于其他上下文，例如从终端主机(end host)到终端主机、跨多条链路的延迟。延迟本身没有正式定义，而是依赖上下文(context-dependent)的。

blocks.en: Timing Diagram
blocks.zh_html: 时序图(Timing Diagram)

blocks.en: Suppose we have a link with bandwidth 1 Mbps = 1 million bits per second, and propagation delay of 1 ms = 0.001 seconds.
blocks.zh_html: 假设我们有一条带宽(bandwidth)为 1 Mbps = 每秒 100 万比特，传播时延(propagation delay)为 1 ms = 0.001 秒的链路(link)。

blocks.en: We want to send a 100 byte = 800 bit packet along this link. How long does it take to send this packet, from the time the first bit is sent, to the time the last bit is received?
blocks.zh_html: 我们想沿着这条链路发送一个 100 字节 = 800 比特的分组(packet)。从发送第一个比特到接收最后一个比特，总共需要多长时间？

blocks.en: To answer this question, we can draw a timing diagram. The left bar is the sender, and the right bar is the recipient. Time starts at 0 and increases as we move down the diagram.
blocks.zh_html: 为了回答这个问题，我们可以画一个时序图(timing diagram)。左侧竖条代表发送方(sender)，右侧竖条代表接收方(recipient)。时间从 0 开始，沿图向下递增。

blocks.en: Let’s focus on the first bit. We can put 1,000,000 bits on the link per second (bandwidth), so it takes 1/1,000,000 = 0.000001 seconds to put a single bit on the link. At time 0.000001 seconds, the link has a single bit on it, at the sender end.
blocks.zh_html: 让我们先关注第一个比特。我们每秒可以在链路上放入 1,000,000 个比特（带宽(bandwidth)），因此将单个比特放到链路上需要 1/1,000,000 = 0.000001 秒。在 0.000001 秒时，链路上有一个比特，位于发送方(sender)一端。

blocks.en: It then takes 0.001 seconds for this bit to travel across the link (propagation delay), so at time 0.000001 + 0.001 seconds, the very first bit arrives at the recipient.
blocks.zh_html: 然后这个比特需要 0.001 秒穿越链路（传播时延(propagation delay)），因此在 0.000001 + 0.001 秒时，第一个比特到达接收方(recipient)。

blocks.en: Now let’s think about the last bit. From before, it takes 0.000001 to put a bit on the link. We have 800 bits to send, so the last bit is placed on the link at time \(800 \cdot 0.000001 = 0.0008\) seconds.
blocks.zh_html: 现在考虑最后一个比特。如前所述，将单个比特放到链路上需要 0.000001 秒。我们要发送 800 个比特，因此最后一个比特在 \(800 \cdot 0.000001 = 0.0008\) 秒时被放到链路上。

blocks.en: It then takes 0.001 seconds for the last bit to travel across the link, so at time 0.0008 + 0.001 seconds, the very last bit arrives at the recipient. This is the time when we can say the packet has arrived at the recipient.
blocks.zh_html: 然后最后一个比特需要 0.001 秒穿越链路，因此在 0.0008 + 0.001 秒时，最后一个比特到达接收方(recipient)。这就是我们可以说分组(packet)已到达接收方的时间。

blocks.en: Packet Delay
blocks.zh_html: 分组时延(Packet Delay)

blocks.en: More generally, the packet delay is the time it takes for an entire packet to be sent, starting from the time the first bit is put on the wire, to the time the last bit is received at the other end. This delay is the sum of the transmission delay and the propagation delay.
blocks.zh_html: 更一般地说，分组时延(packet delay)是发送整个分组(packet)所需的时间，从第一个比特被放到线缆(wire)上开始，到最后一个比特在另一端被接收为止。该时延是传输时延(transmission delay)和传播时延(propagation delay)之和。

blocks.en: The transmission delay tells us how long it takes to put the bits on the wire. In the example, this was \(800 \cdot (1/1{,}000{,}000)\). In general, this is the packet size divided by the link bandwidth.
blocks.zh_html: 传输时延(transmission delay)告诉我们把比特(bits)放到线缆(wire)上需要多长时间。在例子中，这是 \(800 \cdot (1/1{,}000{,}000)\)。一般来说，这是分组大小(packet size)除以链路带宽(link bandwidth)。

blocks.en: Since the transmission delay is a function of bandwidth, we can calculate packet delay in terms of the two link properties of bandwidth and propagation delay.
blocks.zh_html: 由于传输时延(transmission delay)是带宽(bandwidth)的函数，我们可以用带宽和传播时延(propagation delay)这两个链路性质来计算分组时延(packet delay)。

blocks.en: Bandwidth and Propagation Delay Tradeoffs
blocks.zh_html: 带宽与传播时延的权衡(Bandwidth and Propagation Delay Tradeoffs)

blocks.en: Consider two links:
blocks.zh_html: 考虑两条链路(links)：

blocks.en: Link 1 has bandwidth 10 Mbps and propagation delay 10 ms.
blocks.zh_html: 链路 1 的带宽(bandwidth)为 10 Mbps，传播时延(propagation delay)为 10 ms。

blocks.en: Link 2 has bandwidth 1 Mbps and propagation delay 1 ms.
blocks.zh_html: 链路 2 的带宽(bandwidth)为 1 Mbps，传播时延(propagation delay)为 1 ms。

blocks.en: Which link is better? It depends on the packets you’re sending.
blocks.zh_html: 哪条链路更好？这取决于你要发送的分组(packets)。

blocks.en: Suppose we wanted to send a single 10-byte packet. For both links, the time it takes to put one packet on the wire is negligible, and the propagation delay is the dominant source of delay. Link 2 has the shorter propagation delay, so it’s the better choice.
blocks.zh_html: 假设我们要发送一个 10 字节的分组(packet)。对两条链路而言，将一个分组放到线缆上的时间都可以忽略不计，传播时延(propagation delay)是主要时延来源。链路 2 的传播时延更短，因此它是更好的选择。

blocks.en: Suppose we instead wanted to send a single 10,000-byte packet. Now, the transmission delay is the dominant source of delay, and we prefer Link 1, which allows us to put the bytes on the wire faster (higher bandwidth). You could validate this intuition with formal packet delay calculations: Link 1 takes roughly 18 ms to send this packet, while Link 2 takes roughly 81 ms.
blocks.zh_html: 假设我们改为发送一个 10,000 字节的分组(packet)。现在，传输时延(transmission delay)成为主要时延来源，我们更偏好链路 1，因为它允许我们更快地将字节放到线缆上（更高的带宽(bandwidth)）。你可以通过正式的分组时延计算来验证这一直觉：链路 1 发送这个分组大约需要 18 ms，而链路 2 需要大约 81 ms。

blocks.en: For a real-world example, consider a video call. If the video quality is poor, you probably have insufficient bandwidth (and shortening propagation delay won’t help). By contrast, if there’s a delay between the time you speak and the time the other person answers, the propagation delay is probably too long (and more bandwidth won’t help).
blocks.zh_html: 举一个现实世界的例子：视频通话(video call)。如果视频质量很差，很可能是带宽(bandwidth)不足（缩短传播时延(propagation delay)也无济于事）。相反，如果你说话和对方回应之间存在明显延迟，那很可能是传播时延太长（增加带宽也没有帮助）。

blocks.en: Pipe Diagram
blocks.zh_html: 管道图(Pipe Diagram)

blocks.en: So far, we’ve been drawing timing diagrams to denote when network events happen (e.g. when the recipient gets the packet).
blocks.zh_html: 到目前为止，我们一直在用时序图(timing diagrams)来表示网络事件发生的时间，例如接收方(recipient)何时收到分组(packet)。

blocks.en: Another way to view packets being sent across the network is to draw the bits on the link at a frozen moment in time. Both views convey the same information, but depending on the context, one view might be more useful than the other.
blocks.zh_html: 另一种观察分组(packets)在网络上发送的方式是：在某个冻结的时间点，绘制链路上的比特(bits)。两种视角传达的信息相同，但根据上下文，一种视角可能比另一种更有用。

blocks.en: To draw the link, we can imagine the link is a pipe (similar to the water analogy) and draw the pipe as a rectangle, where the width is the propagation delay, and the height is the bandwidth. The area of the pipe is the capacity of the link.
blocks.zh_html: 要绘制链路(link)，我们可以把链路想象成一根管子（类似于水的类比），然后将管子画成一个矩形：宽度是传播时延(propagation delay)，高度是带宽(bandwidth)。管子的面积就是链路的容量(capacity)。

blocks.en: Suppose we want to send a 50-byte packet across the link. In the pipe view, we can show a frozen moment in time with the packet being sent along the link.
blocks.zh_html: 假设我们要通过链路发送一个 50 字节的分组(packet)。在管道视图中，我们可以展示一个冻结的时间点，显示分组正在链路上传输。

blocks.en: The packet is arranged in a rectangle, where the height of the rectangle tells us how many bytes were placed on the wire in a single time step. At every time step, the packet slides right in the pipe. Eventually, the packet starts to exit the pipe, and at each time step, one column of the rectangle exits the pipe.
blocks.zh_html: 分组被表示为一个矩形，矩形的高度告诉我们每个时间步(time step)放到线缆上的字节数。在每个时间步，分组在管道中向右滑动。最终，分组开始离开管道，每个时间步有一列矩形从管道中退出。

blocks.en: Non-obvious fact: The packet transmission delay in the timing diagram corresponds to the width of the rectangle.
blocks.zh_html: 不那么明显的事实：时序图(timing diagram)中的分组传输时延(transmission delay)对应管道图中矩形的宽度。

blocks.en: To see why, suppose we have a link that can send 5 bits per second, and we have a 20-bit packet. In the timing diagram, there are 11 seconds between the time of the first and last bit being sent.
blocks.zh_html: 为了理解原因，假设我们有一条每秒发送 5 个比特(bits)的链路(link)，要发送一个 20 比特的分组(packet)。在时序图(timing diagram)中，第一个比特和最后一个比特发送的时间间隔是 11 秒。

blocks.en: In the pipe diagram, every second, a column of 5 bits marches into the pipe. We need 4 columns to enter the pipe, which takes 4 seconds. This means the width of the packet in the pipe is 4 columns of packets = 4 seconds.
blocks.zh_html: 在管道图(pipe diagram)中，每秒有一列 5 个比特进入管道。我们需要 4 列才能全部进入管道，这需要 4 秒。这意味着分组在管道中的宽度是 4 列 = 4 秒。

blocks.en: The pipe diagram lets us view the packet transmission time on the same axis as the propagation delay, and compare the two terms.
blocks.zh_html: 管道图让我们在同一个轴上看到分组传输时间(packet transmission time)和传播时延(propagation delay)，便于比较这两项。

blocks.en: Pipe diagrams can be useful for comparing different links. Let’s look at the exact same packets traveling through three different links.
blocks.zh_html: 管道图(pipe diagrams)对于比较不同链路(links)很有用。让我们看看完全相同的分组(packets)在三条不同链路中传输的情况。

blocks.en: If we shorten the propagation delay, the pipe width gets shorter. The pipe height stays the same, and the shape of each rectangular packet is the same. (Remember, you can think of the packet height as the number of bits marching into the pipe at each time step, and the packet width as the time it takes to march all bits into the pipe.)
blocks.zh_html: 如果缩短传播时延(propagation delay)，管道宽度变窄。管道高度保持不变，每个矩形分组(packet)的形状也相同。（记住，你可以把分组高度理解为每个时间步进入管道的比特(bits)数，把分组宽度理解为将所有比特送入管道所需的时间。）

blocks.en: Other observations here: The packet width staying the same means the transmission delay didn’t change. Also, the area of the link decreased, which tells us that the link has less capacity.
blocks.zh_html: 其他观察：分组宽度保持不变意味着传输时延(transmission delay)没有改变。此外，链路的面积减小了，说明链路的容量(capacity)变小了。

blocks.en: When we increase the bandwidth, the pipe height gets taller, indicating that we can march more bits into the pipe per unit time.
blocks.zh_html: 增加带宽(bandwidth)时，管道高度变高，表示每单位时间可以往管道中送入更多比特(bits)。

blocks.en: Notice that the shape of the packets also changed. The packets are now taller, because we can march more bits into the pipe per unit time. As a result, we finish feeding the packet into the pipe much faster, so the width of the packets (transmission delay) decreases.
blocks.zh_html: 注意分组(packets)的形状也发生了变化。分组现在更高了，因为我们每单位时间可以向管道中送入更多比特(bits)。结果就是，我们可以更快地把分组送入管道，因此分组的宽度（传输时延(transmission delay)）减小了。

blocks.en: Overloaded Links
blocks.zh_html: 过载链路(Overloaded Links)

blocks.en: Consider this picture of packets arriving at a switch. The switch needs to forward all the packets along the outgoing link. In this case, there’s no problem, because the switch has enough capacity to process every packet as it arrives.
blocks.zh_html: 考虑这幅图：分组(packets)到达交换机(switch)。交换机需要将所有分组从出站链路(outgoing link)转发出去。这种情况下没有问题，因为交换机有足够的容量(capacity)来处理每个到达的分组。

blocks.en: What about in this picture?
blocks.zh_html: 那这幅图呢？

blocks.en: In the long term, we have enough capacity to send all the outgoing packets, but at this very instant in time, we have two packets arriving simultaneously, and we can only send out one. This is called transient overload, and it’s extremely common at switches in the Internet.
blocks.zh_html: 从长期来看，我们有足够的容量(capacity)发送所有出站分组(packets)，但在这一瞬间，有两个分组同时到达，而我们一次只能发送一个。这称为瞬态过载(transient overload)，在互联网(Internet)的交换机(switches)中极其常见。

blocks.en: To cope with transient overload, the switch maintains a queue of packets. If two packets arrive simultaneously, the switch queues one of them and sends out the other one.
blocks.zh_html: 为了应对瞬态过载(transient overload)，交换机(switch)维护一个分组队列(queue)。如果两个分组同时到达，交换机将一个放入队列，发送另一个。

blocks.en: At any given time, the switch could choose to send a packet from one of the incoming links, or send a packet from the queue. This choice is determined by a packet scheduling algorithm, and there are lots of different designs that we’ll look at.
blocks.zh_html: 在任何时刻，交换机(switch)可以选择发送来自某条入站链路(incoming link)的分组，或者发送队列(queue)中的分组。这个选择由分组调度(packet scheduling)算法决定，我们将会看到许多不同的设计。

blocks.en: When there are no incoming packets, the switch can drain the queue and send out any queued packets.
blocks.zh_html: 如果没有入站分组(packets)，交换机(switch)可以清空队列(queue)，发送所有排队的分组。

blocks.en: This allows queues to help us absorb transient bursts.
blocks.zh_html: 这使得队列(queues)可以帮助我们吸收瞬态突发(transient bursts)。

blocks.en: What if the incoming links looked like this?
blocks.zh_html: 如果入站链路(incoming links)是这种情况呢？

blocks.en: Now we have persistent overload. There just isn’t enough capacity on the outgoing link to support the level of incoming traffic.
blocks.zh_html: 现在我们有了持续过载(persistent overload)。出站链路(outgoing link)根本没有足够的容量(capacity)来支撑入站流量(incoming traffic)的水平。

blocks.en: We could fill the queue up, but that still isn’t enough to support the incoming load. One way or another, the switch will drop packets.
blocks.zh_html: 我们可以填满队列(queue)，但这仍然不足以支撑入站负载(incoming load)。无论如何，交换机(switch)都会丢弃分组(packets)。

blocks.en: How do we account for persistent overload? Operators need to properly provision their links and switches. If they notice that a switch is frequently overloaded, they might decide to upgrade the link (which may require manual work).
blocks.zh_html: 如何应对持续过载(persistent overload)？运营方(operators)需要合理规划(provision)他们的链路(links)和交换机(switches)。如果他们发现某个交换机频繁过载，可能会决定升级链路（这可能需要人工操作）。

blocks.en: One possible solution to overload is to have the router tell the senders to slow down. (We’ll study this later when we look at congestion control.) Ultimately, there’s not much we can do to solve overload, though, which is why the Internet is designed to only offer best-effort service.
blocks.zh_html: 过载(overload)的一个可能解决方案是让路由器(router)通知发送方放慢速度。（我们将在拥塞控制(congestion control)章节研究这个问题。）但归根结底，我们对解决过载能做的不多，这也是为什么互联网(Internet)被设计为只提供尽力而为(best-effort)服务。

blocks.en: Now that we have a notion of queuing, we need to go back and update our packet delay formula. Now, packet delay is the sum of transmission delay, propagation delay, and queuing delay.
blocks.zh_html: 既然我们有了排队(queuing)的概念，就需要回过头来更新我们的分组时延(packet delay)公式。现在，分组时延是传输时延(transmission delay)、传播时延(propagation delay)和排队时延(queuing delay)之和。
